title: Organizing an Argument
description: Choose relevant evidence, then use source evidence in a short argument.
subject: rla
author: Studo
reviewer: Retired by Extended Response V1 migration

questions.prompt: Which piece of evidence would most strengthen the case for opening the library on Sundays?

options.text: A survey showing that 40% of working families can only visit on weekends.
A description of the library's current Tuesday hours.
options.whyWrong: Tuesday hours do not show a need for Sunday access.

options.text: The library director's opinion on staffing preferences.
options.whyWrong: Staff preferences do not directly show whether Sunday hours would help the public.

options.text: The number of books in the library's catalog.
options.whyWrong: Catalog size does not tell us whether people need Sunday access.

explanation.whyCorrect: The survey directly shows that many working families need weekend access, so it supports the argument for Sunday hours.
explanation.quickTip: Strong evidence must directly support the exact claim being argued.

questions.prompt: In 3–5 sentences, argue for one side of the debate. Use at least one detail from the passage as evidence.

explanation.whyCorrect: A strong response takes one clear position, uses a specific detail from the passage, and explains how that detail supports the position.
explanation.quickTip: Do not stop after quoting evidence. Explain why the evidence helps your argument.

curriculum.learningObjective: Choose evidence that is directly relevant to a claim and explain why it strengthens the argument.
